I farm small land, and at my age I will keep the plan simple, familiar, and low-risk. I have 50 years of experience, only 4.1 mu, and well irrigation, so I do not need to gamble on complicated changes. I will keep most of the land in my usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to secure grain from the same field, and I will leave a smaller part for cotton because I already know how to manage it and it gives me some cash income. I will use improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, and improved cotton seed, because on a small farm I care more about stable emergence and yield than saving a little on seed. I will not push fertilizer too hard because excessive input is not worth it for my scale, but I will still feed maize more heavily than wheat and cotton because maize responds strongly. With irrigation from the well, I will water at the key stages instead of too often. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier and fits a small household with limited labor. I will also keep pesticide use moderate: enough to avoid obvious loss, but not excessive. That is the way I would manage this year to balance labor, cost, and stable harvest.
